finding.summary: Speculative generality: StorageBackend ABC, a _REGISTRY with register_backend, and a GCSBackend whose put/get only raise NotImplementedError, all serving one caller (export_transcript at the bottom) that hard-codes 's3'. Selecting 'gcs' from the registry crashes at runtime, and S3Backend's hooks and retry_policy constructor args are stored and never used.
S3Backend accepts hooks and retry_policy in its constructor but never uses them, which suggests retry behaviour that does not exist.
register_backend mutates the module-level _REGISTRY dict with no locking, so concurrent registration from several threads could corrupt or race the registry.
EmbeddingClient is a single-implementation class with no interface; this is speculative abstraction over boto3 and should be inlined at the call sites.
emit() wraps everything in a broad except Exception, which swallows serialization errors and hides logging failures.
useDebounced.ts has duplicate and unused imports (useRef, ReactNode) and mixes single and double quotes and semicolons.

store.ts now reads SESSIONS_TABLE with a fallback to 'agent-sessions-dev', but infra/ecs/agent-task.json still sets SESSION_TABLE=agent-sessions-prod. In production the new variable is unset, the fallback silently applies, and live sessions are written to and read from the dev table instead of failing fast.
The `?? 'agent-sessions-dev'` default is dangerous: if the environment variable is ever missing in production the service will quietly use the dev table.
Dropping the non-null assertion makes TABLE typed string | undefined, so passing it as TableName to PutCommand and GetCommand will fail TypeScript compilation.
names.py imports os, sys and Optional without using them, has unsorted imports and mixed quote styles.
BlobStore Protocol plus two store classes is over-engineered; store_for could pick between two plain functions without an abstraction.

The web handler now imports agent.internal.db_models and agent.internal.engine and queries and deletes SessionRow directly, bypassing agent.api. This is a module-boundary and layering violation, not an in-function craft issue.

The per-record catch logs and swallows every error, so the handler resolves normally and Lambda reports the whole batch as successful; SQS deletes the failed messages too. The DLQ redrive policy (maxReceiveCount = 3 in ingest-queue.tf) can never trigger, so failed ingests are lost with only a log line. It should rethrow or return batchItemFailures.
The catch block swallows errors, which is bad practice.
Promise.all rejects as soon as one record fails, aborting the other in-flight ingests of the batch and leaving them half-processed.
EMBED_MAX_INPUTS = 96 is a magic number that should come from configuration.

getUserSettings reads but also writes a default row to DynamoDB on a miss (PutCommand), and it is called from GET handlers, so a read-only request creates data. Two concurrent first reads race and the loser throws ConditionalCheckFailedException, turning a GET into a 500. It should be named getOrCreate or the create moved to a separate path.
The name getUserSettings is misleading because the method also creates a row when none exists.
DEFAULTS is declared `as const`, so its readonly literal types make `{ userId, ...DEFAULTS }` not assignable to UserSettings and the code will not compile.
tenant_id and the title filter are concatenated into the SQL string, which allows SQL injection and bypass of tenant scoping.

process_document nests six levels deep and takes four overlapping boolean flags (embed, persist, dry_run, legacy). Callers pass them positionally, so backfill's process_document(doc, True, False, True, True) is unreadable and easy to invert. Some combinations (embed=False with persist=True) save None vectors into the vector column.
process_document has too many parameters and too much nesting; refactor it.
handler() calls process_document and discards its return value, so the processed chunks are never persisted and the ingest Lambda does nothing useful.
Adding the pgvector package is an unnecessary new dependency; the previous str(vec) cast worked without it.

Money and tokens travel as bare numbers with no units. PRICE_PER_MTOK = 300 states no currency, but the computed cost is passed to record_usage(cost_usd) and stored as dollars; if 300 is cents the stored spend is 100x too high. The budget check compares against an unnamed magic 5000 whose unit is not stated, and cost is persisted as str(float). Named constants or a Money/Cents type are needed.
The budget threshold 5000 in run_turn is an unnamed magic number and its unit is unclear.
record_usage is called just before the budget check, so tenant.spent_today already includes this turn's cost and `spent_today + cost` double counts it.

ReadOnlyToolRegistry subclasses ToolRegistry only to reuse get/names and overrides register() to raise, which strengthens the base contract (Liskov violation). build_registry still passes the instance to plugin.install(reg) for each discovered plugin; any plugin that registers a tool hits PermissionError, so the sandbox profile crashes at boot. A read-only view wrapping a registry would fit better.
ReadOnlyToolRegistry overrides register() to raise PermissionError, violating the Liskov substitution principle; prefer composition.
ReadOnlyToolRegistry.__init__ calls self._tools.update(tools), so the caller's BASE_TOOLS dict is shared and later mutated through the registry, defeating the read-only guarantee.
ingest_document does parsing, cleaning, chunking, embedding and persistence in one function, violating the single responsibility principle.
include_archived is a boolean flag argument that switches behaviour; split list_documents into list_active and list_all functions.

AgentTool is a fat interface (schema, validate, execute, stream, cancel, estimateCost) and both tools stub what they do not support: stream() throws, cancel is a no-op and estimateCost returns 0. Any caller that calls stream() on a non-streaming tool through the AgentTool type gets a runtime throw the types cannot predict, and every new simple tool must repeat the stubs (interface segregation).
The AgentTool interface is too large.
name and description are mutable public class fields on the tools; they should be readonly.
The `?? 'info'` and `?? '15000'` defaults in config silently hide missing configuration, the same fallback pattern that mixes environments.
toPublicProject and toAdminProject are identical, and so are the two list functions; merge them into one to remove duplication.

ReportService.submit does validation, SQL persistence, HTML email layout and SES delivery in one method. Validation rules, schema, email styling and transport change for different reasons, and testing validation needs a DB and SES. A failure in send_email after the insert leaves a saved report with no notification and no way to retry only the notify step.
If ses.send_email fails after the row is inserted, the report is saved but on-call is never notified and there is no retry.
payload['ticket'] at insert time raises KeyError when the ticket key is absent, giving a 500 instead of a validation error.
claim() catches ClientError and returns False, swallowing errors from DynamoDB.

The tests only assert that a mock was called, that a result is not None, and that a mock returns its configured value (the third test patches apply_discount itself), so they pass even if apply_discount is wrong.

The EmbeddingProvider interface and the argument-less EmbeddingProviderFactory.create() wrap exactly one implementation (BedrockTitanProvider) with a single caller (chunker.ts). The factory cannot choose anything and no second provider or test double exists, so this adds three indirections of speculative abstraction.
A class with only a static create method is unnecessary; the factory should be a plain function.
chunker.ts now builds the provider at module scope on import, which can run before AWS configuration is available; the old code created the client lazily.
The first test patches summarize_ticket itself and asserts on the mock, the empty-ticket test has no assertion, and the truncation test ends with `assert True`, so none of them can fail.
tenant_id, title and owner are interpolated into the SQL text with % formatting, so user input allows SQL injection and tenant scoping can be bypassed.
The isolation suite is vacuous: `len(rows) >= 0` and `or True` can never fail, the one real cross-tenant test is skipped, and seeding relies on module-level shared state plus sleep.

dispatch_tool turns a JSONDecodeError (truncated or malformed tool_use input) into args = {} instead of returning an error to the model. Combined with the new default scope='all' on clear_memory, a garbled clear_memory call runs with no arguments, takes the else branch, deletes the user's entire memory, and returns 'memory cleared', so the model sees success.
Catching JSONDecodeError and substituting empty arguments hides malformed model output instead of surfacing it.
Giving clear_memory a default scope='all' makes the `scope == 'topic' and topic` branch unreachable, so topic-level deletion no longer works.
Wrapping psycopg.Error in DocumentRepositoryError hides the original database error and traceback from callers.

Adds the requests dependency (pyproject.toml) for a single GET although httpx is already a declared dependency and is used two lines above in probes.py. It also turns the async probe into a blocking requests.get inside the async readiness endpoint, stalling the event loop for up to 3s per health check.
requests is a redundant new dependency when httpx already exists.
probe_ticket_api is now synchronous but readiness() calls it without await, so tickets is an unawaited coroutine that is always truthy and the check never fails.
The download endpoint signs any caller-supplied S3 key without checking it belongs to the caller's tenant, so one tenant can fetch another tenant's documents (IDOR).

On any exception the handler re-sends the whole message to the queue, so a failure in send_receipt after charge_customer charges the customer again. There is no idempotency key, backoff, max attempts or DLQ, and the handler never reports partial batch failure.

AnswerService.answer builds its own psycopg connection and anthropic.Anthropic client from environment variables inside the method, while SummaryService in the same diff receives db and llm through its constructor. The logic cannot be unit-tested without a live database and API credentials, a new connection is opened per call, and changing the DSN or provider means editing the service.
AnswerService should use dependency injection.
The connection is closed in the finally block before rows are consumed, so building context from rows afterwards is a use-after-close error.
The function name requeue_dead_letter_messages_older_than_one_hour is far too long; use a shorter name such as requeue_dlq.
The switch statements on RunStatus violate the open/closed principle; replace them with a lookup map or polymorphism.

listOrdersForTeam is a copy of listOrdersForUser that has already diverged: it omits the `deleted_at is null` filter and returns all PAGE+1 rows without slicing. Team views show soft-deleted orders, each page has 51 items, and nextCursor comes from the 51st row so that item is skipped on the next page. A shared paging helper is needed.
listOrdersForUser and listOrdersForTeam are near-duplicates; extract a shared pagination helper.
In listOrdersForUser the nextCursor is taken from the last sliced item, so the 51st row that was fetched is dropped and never returned on the next page.

The new `except Exception` in search_chunks turns any embedding outage, pgvector timeout or SQL error into an empty list. knowledge_search renders an empty list as 'nothing on this topic' and tells the agent to relay that to the user, so during an incident Claude confidently says the knowledge base has no information, with only a warning log line.
The broad except Exception returning [] hides failures behind an empty result, with only a warning logged.
The return statement sits inside the `async with pool.connection()` block within the try, so when an exception occurs the pooled connection is never released and the pool leaks.

The web route imports underscore-private _pool and _MEMORY_COLUMNS from agent.internal.memory_store and issues SQL against the agent's agent_memory table, bypassing the service API. This is a module-boundary violation.

CachedRetriever narrows the Retriever contract: search raises NotImplementedError for any filters and ValueError for k > 20, while the base accepts both. knowledge_tool calls retriever.search(query, k=50, filters={'tenant': ...}) and build_retriever now returns CachedRetriever, so every knowledge-tool call fails at runtime. Dropping the filters instead would leak other tenants' chunks.
CachedRetriever.search raises ValueError when k > 20, which the Retriever base allows; this violates substitutability.
`if hit:` treats a cached empty result (the stored JSON string '[]') as falsy, so empty searches are never served from cache and always hit the inner retriever.
withThrottleRetry catches every error in a generic try/catch, which can swallow real failures from DynamoDB writes.

Dispatcher switches on msg.kind and inlines the Slack and PagerDuty fetch calls even though the diff introduces a Channel interface with EmailChannel as the precedent. Each new channel means editing Dispatcher and the kind union, an unhandled kind silently does nothing because there is no default, and the global fetch calls cannot be stubbed in tests.
The switch in Dispatcher is not extensible and violates the open/closed principle.
The slack case has no break before the pagerduty case, so a Slack alert falls through and also fires a PagerDuty event.

The handler replaces the queue-decoupled 202 flow with an inline poll loop of up to 28s in the API Lambda while the agent worker is invoked async. Turns that exceed API Gateway's 29s limit return 504 while the Lambda is billed for waiting; this is a system topology and async-flow problem.

get_tool_config does a shallow merge, so cfg['allowed_tools'] is the very list inside DEFAULT_CONFIG for tenants without that override, and it is cached. The runner's .append('refund_issue') for support agents mutates that shared list in place, so afterwards every tenant and every non-support user sees refund_issue as allowed.
The runner mutates the cfg dict returned from the cache, which can leak state into other requests.
Renaming DEFAULT_TOOLS to DEFAULT_CONFIG is gratuitous churn unrelated to the feature.
